title: RV-03 review: Secure multi-application production layout
rationale: The layout correctly separates application Compose services from shared platform services, but the backup implementation requests a global PostgreSQL dump using only the application runtime role and the changed migration instructions omit the required isolated rehearsal before restoring production targets. Both gaps affect a production-availability/data-preservation change.
scope_architecture: The Compose split, release installation, backup/restore scripts, systemd units, and migration runbooks all change production topology and durable-data recovery behavior. Keeping PostgreSQL, Grafana, and Ollama platform-owned is architecturally correct, but it raises the required availability and recovery evidence rather than removing it.

findings.finding: The application backup invokes pg_dumpall for global objects using the application runtime environment, although the new production layout intentionally supplies only a dedicated application database role.
findings.evidence: The runbook assigns the application database/role to the application and keeps shared platform administration separate. pg_dumpall --globals-only reads cluster-global roles and configuration, which an application role is not expected to administer; no separate approved platform backup credential or platform-owned backup path is supplied.
findings.impact: Daily and weekly backup runs can fail before producing a verified recovery set, leaving the deployment without the backup evidence required for migration and availability changes.
findings.required_change: Remove the global dump from the application-owned backup or make it an explicitly platform-owned operation with its own approved least-privilege execution path; exercise the selected path with the actual application role.
findings.suggested_test: Run the daily and weekly backup commands against an isolated shared-platform PostgreSQL instance using the configured application role, then verify SHA256SUMS and the resulting restore set.

findings.finding: The changed migration runbook proceeds from empty production targets directly to restore and service startup without an isolated rehearsal procedure or recorded rehearsal result.
findings.evidence: The diff's migration section says to confirm the target directories and database are empty and then run restore/start. The task has production_availability and data_loss_migration flags, for which the matrix requires isolated recovery/rehearsal, rollback, and post-rollback health/data evidence; the fixture supplies only a generic bounded review.
findings.impact: A first recovery attempt can discover an incompatible dump, permissions, network, Compose, or startup failure against the production target, risking extended outage or loss of the safe rollback boundary.
findings.required_change: Add a bounded, isolated rehearsal procedure using separate project, paths, credentials, loopback ports, and disabled external export; record its restore, health, data comparison, rollback, and shared-service non-interference results before cutover.
findings.suggested_test: Run an isolated migration rehearsal from a checksummed candidate set and verify restore counts, representative hashes, readiness, rollback, and zero external export.

contract_consumer_review: The changed consumers are application Compose, systemd, release installation, migration/backup tooling, the application database role, and platform-owned services. The diff removes application lifecycle management for shared services, but backup and recovery remain cross-owner contracts and must be tested with the actual separation.

evidence_matrix.check: Approved fixture brief and pinned diff identity
Historical Compose, release, and security checks supplied in implementation report
Application-role backup and isolated restore rehearsal

operations_safety_security_privacy: The intended ownership boundary avoids application management of shared services and keeps the runtime secret separate. The missing executable backup/rehearsal proof remains a high-risk operational gap; no production access was used to infer success.
documentation_assessment: The revised runbook documents checksums and rollback intent, but it lacks the required isolated rehearsal gate before the production restore/start commands.
limitations: Historical automated/manual PASS statements were reviewed as supplied; no production credentials, service topology, backup archive, or rehearsal environment was accessed.
The review did not execute destructive restore or Compose operations.
